issue.title: actstat and bob-cli generated agent docs still carry Tier 1/Tier 2 headings and type:/parent: web descriptors after epic sase-vk
issue.description:
Proposed by phase bead sase-vk.3 (note 1) while landing epic sase-vk (plan:202608/memory_webs_agents_section.md). The epic plan's "Out of scope" section named this explicitly and scoped it out of every phase, because the regeneration must run against an installed `sase` that already carries the epic's commits.

VERIFIED, not inherited. Opened both projects with `/sase_repo` at actstat 6534ffc and bob-cli f1723a3 (both clean, both last regenerated by `chore: run sase init memory`) and confirmed two independent kinds of drift.

1. Section headings. Both AGENTS.md files still open with `## 1. Tier 1 (core) Memory` and `## 2. Tier 2 (reference) Memory`. Epic sase-vk renamed these to `## Core Memory` / `## Memory Webs` / `## Reference Memory` with no tier vocabulary anywhere. The provider shims (CLAUDE.md, GEMINI.md, QWEN.md, OPENCODE.md) are byte-copies of AGENTS.md, so each carries the same stale headings.

2. Web descriptor frontmatter. Epic sase-vk made a web descriptor declare no `type:` and no `parent:`, and taught `sase memory init` to strip both on convergence. Both projects still have them committed: actstat's `sase/memory/task_types.md` carries `type: core` and `parent: AGENTS.md`; bob-cli's `sase/memory/glossary.md` carries `type: core` and its `sase/memory/task_types.md` carries both keys.

Neither is a defect in sase itself and neither self-corrects: the drift persists until `sase memory init` runs in each project against a sase build containing 1be5429ea, b726d0a18, and 0860fcb20. `sase memory init --check` in each project should report the drift, and a single `sase memory init` run should converge both the headings and the descriptor frontmatter in one pass.

Impact: an agent working in actstat or bob-cli reads always-loaded instructions written in vocabulary that no longer exists anywhere in sase, and the /sase_memory_read skill it is told to use now describes a different placement rule than its own AGENTS.md shows.

task_type_fields.path: AGENTS.md and sase/memory/*.md web descriptors in the actstat and bob-cli projects (not this repo)
task_type_fields.proposed_change: Run `sase memory init` in actstat and in bob-cli from a sase install that carries epic sase-vk (commits 1be5429ea, b726d0a18, 0860fcb20), then commit the regenerated AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, GEMINI.md, QWEN.md, OPENCODE.md, sase/memory/README.md, and the migrated web descriptors in each project. Confirm `sase memory init --check` is clean on a second pass in both, and that neither AGENTS.md contains the string "Tier".

payload.description: Same defect shape, same two projects: a sase-side change lands and actstat/bob-cli keep serving stale generated memory until sase memory init reruns there. sase-tq was the feature task-type snapshot; sase-vv is epic sase-vk's tier rename.

Likely mechanism: the global sase on PATH is a uv tool install pinned to a separate checkout, so a regeneration run there can lag the commits it should carry. Confirm that install is current before running sase memory init.
adjacent generated-AGENTS.md heading drift, different surface

payload.close_reason: Both projects have already run the requested regeneration: bob-cli commit 361a165 (2026-09-03) and actstat commit a231a01 (2026-09-05). Their current AGENTS.md files use Core Memory, Reference Memory and Memory Webs, with no Tier 1/Tier 2 headings; all four provider shims were regenerated in the same commits. Those commits also update the web descriptors, including bob-cli glossary and both task_types descriptors. The stale revisions f1723a3/6534ffc in this task are no longer current; rerunning this migration as a separate task would be redundant.
